ingredient_evidence.claim: CIR Expert Panel concluded that phenoxyethanol is safe as a cosmetic ingredient in the present practices of use and concentration; in clinical studies it was neither a primary irritant nor a sensitizer. The Panel later declined to reopen the assessment (2007). This is safety evidence, not evidence that phenoxyethanol is suitable for a particular facial skin type.
ingredient_evidence.citation: Final Report on the Safety Assessment of Phenoxyethanol. J Am Coll Toxicol. 1990;9(2):259-277. DOI 10.3109/10915819009078737

ingredient_evidence.claim: SCCS opinion: 2-phenoxyethanol is safe for use as a preservative with a maximum concentration of 1.0% in cosmetic products, including for children (exposure from non-cosmetic sources not considered). This is safety evidence, not evidence of suitability for a particular facial skin type.
ingredient_evidence.source_name: Scientific Committee on Consumer Safety (SCCS), European Commission
ingredient_evidence.citation: SCCS Opinion on Phenoxyethanol, SCCS/1575/16, adopted 6 October 2016

ingredient_evidence.claim: CIR Expert Panel concluded that chlorphenesin is safe in the present practices of use and concentration (reported use up to 0.3% in leave-on and 0.32% in rinse-off products). Dermal absorption was high in rats but available data showed an absence of toxicity. This is safety evidence, not evidence of suitability for a particular facial skin type.
ingredient_evidence.citation: Johnson W Jr et al. Safety Assessment of Chlorphenesin as Used in Cosmetics. Int J Toxicol. 2014;33(2 Suppl):5S-15S. PMID 24861369. DOI 10.1177/1091581814526893
